# pcd_identity_federation_mapping (Resource)

Manages a Keystone federation mapping: the rules that turn the attributes a SAML identity provider asserts into a local user name, email and group. In PCD single sign-on, one mapping holds one rule per SSO group, and the `saml2` protocol of the identity provider points at it (`pcd_identity_federation_protocol`); the PCD UI names it `<identity provider, lowercase>_mapping`, for example `idp1_mapping`. The SSO guide shows the whole setup.

The resource owns the whole rule list: editing the SAML groups in the PCD UI rewrites the same mapping, and the next apply puts the configured rules back. Keystone also stores a `schema_version` for each mapping, which this resource does not manage: every create and update gets Keystone's default. Destroying a mapping that a protocol still names succeeds (Keystone does not check), and single sign-on through that protocol then fails until it names another mapping.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "pcd_identity_group" "sso_admins" {
  name = "sso-admins"
}

# One rule per SSO group, in the shape the PCD UI writes: a user who signs in
# gets their email address as user name and email, and joins sso-admins when
# the identity provider lists them in its "pcd-admins" group. "email" and
# "groups" are the ids the SSO configuration's attribute map gives the SAML
# attributes.
resource "pcd_identity_federation_mapping" "idp1" {
  name = "idp1_mapping"
  rules = jsonencode([{
    local = [{
      user  = { name = "{0}", email = "{1}" }
      group = { id = pcd_identity_group.sso_admins.id }
    }]
    remote = [
      { type = "email" },
      { type = "email" },
      { type = "groups", any_one_of = ["pcd-admins"] },
    ]
  }])
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The mapping's ID in Keystone, 1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens: a protocol's `mapping_id` can name nothing else. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `rules` (String) The mapping rules, a JSON array in Keystone's mapping language; build it with `jsonencode([...])`. Every key is sent as written. Name groups as `pcd_identity_group.<name>.id`, not as literal IDs: the reference makes Terraform destroy the mapping before the groups it names. Updated in place.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The mapping name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax. The IDs are assigned by PCD; the
[Importing guide](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/platform9/pcd/latest/docs/guides/importing)
explains how to look them up.

```shell
# The mapping name: pcdctl mapping list
terraform import pcd_identity_federation_mapping.idp1 idp1_mapping
```
